AFFORDABLE JAPANESE SET MEALS
Nov 2022
Fujiro is all about Tonkatsu set meals, and they do it very well. The restaurant is located in alley 8A Thai Van Lung, go in and turn left and you will see Fujiro right under Moon Spa. They have very authentic Japanese-style pork chop rice and chicken too. Recommended when you want to eat heartily as the pork cutlets are like 2.5cm thick. Since it’s incredibly popular at lunchtime, drop by in the middle of the day to snag a seat. The only downside here will be their staff who spend most of their time talking at the top of their voices and not responsive when you call them.

Awesome Jap pork, Kuro-buta, now at D7 too
Oct 2019
They specialize mainly in pork, especially with the kurobuta black pig as their star dish. Never knew pork can be so moist, juicy, thick and yet tender. Even their rice is awesomely delicious. The most popular dish is pork+egg on a 'hotplate', and the fact that it is constantly hot makes it truly satisfying to savour till the last bite. They also have chicken, salmon, seafood, salads if other members in your group prefer other types of dishes. Their only item on the kids' menu is a pork set.

Their new outlet at District 7 is busy most weekends, and the free mini soft-play playground with glass windows that parents can watch the kids while they eat is probably the reason why it's been drawing throngs of families with young children... and also the fact that their prices are pretty good too!

Service is great, meals are fairly priced
Jan 2019 • Solo
I ordered the egg katsu set and upsized to a medium for an extra 15,000 VND. The service was quick and attentive. The menu is in Japanese, however there are photos for illustrative purposes. The set included a large portion of egg katsu, with the katsu itself being 3cm thick (super thick!) as well as 2 small sides and miso soup. Unfortunately there was too much sauce which overpowered the dish and made it much more soggier than it should have been. The set and a can of coke cost approximately 171,000 VND. The restaurant is tucked away in the few small alleys packed with Japanese restaurants.

Great food with some quirks
Nov 2018 • Couples
Great Japanese restaurant with cute little quirks that enhances the experience; such as grinding your own sesame and mixing it with their special sauce.

The flavours were really good and their wasabi is tasty 😋. There are only a few vegetarian options so maybe not a perfect fit if you are looking to get lost in options. 

We went here during the downtime of Japantown, but I can imagine this place being full during the evenings or lunchtime! 🥢
